profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the westernmost row of the campus, second from the south among five buildings arranged along that row. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure within the campus, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from the campus-wide totals above.

reading.body:
Compass Datacenters is developing Red Oak, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County south of Dallas-Fort Worth, as a 360 megawatt build-out across multiple buildings. This facility sits in the westernmost row of the campus, second from the south. The operator's April 2024 announcement of a 200 million dollar expansion adding two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet indicates the campus remains under active construction.

No per-building capacity figure is published for this specific structure, so its share of the campus-wide 360 megawatt target cannot be assigned. At typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, a full 360 megawatt campus would support roughly 9,000 racks of accelerator hardware, but the actual mix and deployment state of the Red Oak buildings remain unpublished. The campus as a whole is not yet ranked among Texas's published-capacity facilities, as no single confirmed figure for current operational capacity could be verified from operator sources.

Red Oak is one of 133 mapped data center facilities across Texas, but only 18 publish power specifications, totaling 468 megawatts. Once the Red Oak campus reaches its stated 360 megawatt build-out and publishes figures, it would represent roughly 77 percent of Texas's currently published capacity and shift the state's ranking substantially. The timeline and occupancy status of that transition remain unpublished.
